events.title: Michael Kessler: All Resin
events.description:
Michael Kessler has spent decades exploring the boundary between gesture and geometry, and his resin works bring that inquiry into sharper focus than ever.

Each painting is built from up to fifty micro-thin translucent layers, fused and accumulated until something luminous emerges. Biomorphic forms weave through geometric structures, nature's logic made visible through an almost meditative process of application and restraint. Kessler likens his gestural freedom to a kind of painterly tai chi, controlled, but never rigid.

In his all-resin works, that layered depth takes on new dimension. Light travels through the surface rather than simply reflecting off it, making each piece feel as much like a living object as a painting.

Join us August 7th to experience new works by Michael Kessler at Gallery MAR, Park City....

events.title: Matt Flint: Sleeping in the Forest
events.description:
Matt Flint doesn't begin with a plan. No sketches, no predetermined composition, just canvas, paint, and a process as intuitive as the landscapes that shaped him.

Raised in rural Missouri and now living in Wyoming's Wind River Mountains, Flint has spent a lifetime in close study of the natural world, its textures, its rhythms, its constant state of becoming. That attention finds its way into every surface he paints. His works build through layers of creation and destruction, each image emerging as another recedes, holding the tension between what was and what might come next.

The result is painting that moves the way wilderness does, familiar and elusive at once, inviting you closer while always suggesting there's something just beyond the next ridge.

Join us September 5th to experience new works by Matt Flint at Gallery MAR, Park City....

Summit County has a limited number of gloves and wire cutters to borrow.

Hazards may include cuts, punctures, scrapes, tripping, heavy lifting, sharp edges, and exposure to rusted metal or other environmental risks. By signing up and attending this activity, you acknowledge these risks, accept full responsibility for your participation, and agree to the terms of the waiver. A recent tetanus vaccination is recommended, though it is not required. Your safety is our priority—please work carefully, follow instructions, and look out for one another.

events.description:
Join us October 23rd to kick off our first show of the fall, and experience new works by Miles Glynn at Gallery MAR, Park City.

Miles Glynn grew up seeing the American West through a car window, the son of an Army photojournalist, trained from childhood to see the world in frames and compositions. That eye never left him.

Working from Marfa, Texas, Glynn builds layered mixed-media paintings from vintage photographs, forgotten advertising, and Western ephemera, combining silkscreen, paint, and collage into works that feel at once deeply familiar and entirely new. The textures of deteriorating buildings, weathered billboards, and desert landscapes find their way into every surface,  documents of time, resilience, and the stories that linger after everything else fades.

His work doesn't ask you to see what he sees. It asks you to find what only you would....

Joining them is Vertical Horizon, the multi-platinum band behind massive radio hits “Everything You Want,” “You’re a God,” and “Best I Ever Had.” Their emotionally driven songwriting and polished rock sound helped define an era of modern alternative and continue to resonate with audiences today.
Together, these two beloved bands deliver a hit-packed night of nostalgia, sing-along anthems, and timeless alternative rock. Whether you grew up with these songs or discovered them later, this show promises a high-energy, feel-good concert experience you won’t want to miss.

events.title: Dylan Scott
events.description: ABOUT DYLAN SCOTT:Despite a multi-Platinum story and six No. 1 singles, including two fresh smashes in 2025 alone, Curb Records hitmaker Dylan Scott has always kept an underdog mindset. A rowdy roughneck with a romantic side – one whose modern edge was sharpened by timeless, emotional twang – the consummate family man broke out with the epic triple-Platinum devotion of “My Girl” in 2016 and followed up with scrappy, under-the-radar consistency. Chart-topping heart-forward anthems like “Hooked,” “Nobody” and “New Truck” all reached RIAA-certified status, but last year launched the crooner into the stratosphere. Posting back-to-back No. 1s with Gold-certified “Boys Back Home” (with Dylan Marlowe) and Platinum-certified “This Town’s Been Too Good to Us,” Scott wrapped 2025 as the third most-played country artist of 2025 and continues his hot streak with his current single, Platinum-certified “What He’ll Never Have,” which nears the Top 10 at Country radio and was honored by ASCAP as one of the most-performed country songs of 2025. With nearly 5 billion career streams, legions of fans and countless sold-out shows to his credit, his stardom has somehow grown in relative stealth. But with his third full album, Easy Does It, he’s not sweating. Sure of himself, his talent and his fans, Scott heads toward a new creative chapter with total confidence. Featuring 11 tracks, his signature vocal and vivid intensity take center stage on a set defined by personal truth – whether through heartbreak, romantic devotion or small-town dedication. The in-demand live act spent last year on his Country Till I Die Tour, headlining his biggest venues yet including his first-ever arenas and record-breaking attendance, and his Easy Does It Tour. He will continue headlining across the country on his Till I Can’t I Will Tour, launching this spring.

Now breaking into the mainstream with a one-of-a-kind blend of island reggae and country soul, Hawaiian-born rising star Maoli is bringing his people—and his sound—to the world like never before.
The golden-voiced native of upcountry Maui has released nine independent albums, earned over half a billion global streams, and spent nearly 15 years touring and recording, becoming a major fixture across the Pacific Islands and beyond. Inspired by traditional Hawaiian music (the birthplace of the steel guitar), reggae, rock, and country legends like Dolly Parton, Willie Nelson, and George Strait, Maoli has built a signature style that connects Polynesia to the American West Coast—and all the way to Texas.
With a growing global fanbase, Maoli’s Hawaiian-country sound has fueled viral hits and powerful covers, including Brett Young’s “Mercy” (18+ million Spotify streams) and “In Case You Didn’t Know” (10+ million Spotify streams). Now teaming up with hit producers Dann and David Huff, Maoli continues bridging the gap between island soul and country tradition with his latest release, Last Sip of Summer (Island Vibe Edition)—out now.

events.title: Debra Fotheringham
events.description:
Debra Fotheringham is a seasoned singer-songwriter, guitarist, and percussionist whose voice has long been a quietly powerful force in the Utah music scene. Based in Salt Lake City, she’s spent over two decades crafting songs that balance soul-baring vulnerability with refined musicianship. With three studio albums already under her belt, Debra released her fourth this October—her most ambitious and daring work to date.

A founding member of the beloved roots/gospel collective The Lower Lights, Debra’s voice carries both the warmth of tradition and the spark of innovation. Her haunting vocal work has been featured on television networks like PBS, AMC, and The CW, and she’s a recurring collaborator with electronic music luminary Kaskade, contributing to multiple albums including his Grammy-nominated Atmosphere.

Equal parts storyteller and sonic explorer, Debra Fotheringham continues to shape a career that bridges genres and generations—always rooted in authenticity, always reaching for something deeper....

events.title: Gorgeous Gourds
events.description:
Psychedelic Funk band Gorgeous Gourds combine smooth harmonies, deep tasty grooves, and original songwriting.

The Gorgeous Gourd's just released album \(2/22/22\) "Peace and Love" reminds us why we go see and hear live music. The band has evolved to a rock solid synergistic group of accomplished musicians. Their powerful singing and songwriting is evident on their new CD, with 14 worthy cuts combining an eclectic combination of psychedelic funk, folk, tasty jam grooves, smooth harmonies and soulful ballads. Fred, Lucas, and Sarah all share the artful original songwriting. Iconic KRCL DJ John Florence commented on the new album, "Not a stinker in the bunch!”

Formed in Salt Lake City, Utah in 2015, founding members are Fred Hayes \(bass, vocals\), and the strong and steady Bob Smith \(drums\). Lucas Jones \(lead guitar,vocals\) provides sublime and powerful guitar licks and vocals, together with the guitar of Jacob Dahlberg and the dazzling vocals of Heather McCartin. 

Whether you enjoy easing into a bluesy flow ride, or getting all the kinks out on the dance floor, the Gorgeous Gourds is the party you'll keep coming back to. The title of their new album "Peace and Love" is a message they spread with unbridled energy and enthusiasm.

Like they say, "You're Gorgeous, we're the Gourds. Together we are Gorgeous Gourds."

events.title: movies under the stars: the road to patagonia
events.description: MOVIES UNDER THE STARS: the road to patagonia Tuesday, August 4th | Gates 7:30 pm, LIVE MUSIC BY JIM FISH STARTING AT 7:30 pm | Movie at 8:30 pm | Alta Peruvian Back Lawn│$15 | Tickets | Kids Under 5 are FREE THE ROAD TO PATAGONIA Is a stunning, intimate and unflinching series of love letters within a documentary - firstly, a love between two people, and secondly between humanity and the Earth. Ecologist Matty Hannon begins an incredible solo adventure, to surf the west coast of the Americas by motorbike, from the top of Alaska to the tip of Patagonia. But deep in the wilderness - alone with the wolves and the bears - the journeyer's plans unexpectedly fall to pieces. After losing everything, and on the cusp of quitting, he meets the girl of his dreams, a permaculture farmer named Heather. Shot over 16 years, the result is an adventurous exposé on the more-than-human-world, offering a physical and spiritual odyssey to better understand our place in Nature. Winner - Best Film and Best Documentary - Byron Bay International Film Festival Winner Audience Choice Award - Florida Surf Film Festival Winner Audience Choice Award - Melbourne Documentary Film Festival FACTS & TIPS: You must bring your own LOW chairs and they must be 31.5" height or less. Or blankets to sit on. Picnic dinners are allowed. NO GRILLS. If two separate households would like to be near each other we recommend arriving at the same time. No dogs, unless tagged by the Town of Alta or an ADA service dog. Prepare for chilly mountain evenings, bring blankets and layers. If you have questions regarding accessibility to our events, please contact  Sara Gibbs, Executive Director. ACE aims to create an inclusive and accessible environment for all of our attendees; please contact our Executive Director, Sara Gibbs, with any questions regarding accessibility...

events.title: Haydn, Mendelssohn, & A Viola Concerto
events.description: The rich voice of the viola takes center stage as Utah Symphony Principal Viola Brant Bayless performs Dai Fujikura's Wayfinder, a concerto inspired by Polynesian navigation traditions. In this imaginative work, the orchestra becomes the natural forces used to find direction—stars, winds, and ocean swells—while the soloist listens and charts a path forward through shifting musical currents.Like a musical guide through the evening, Maurice Cohn conducts a program that unfolds across vivid sonic landscapes, beginning with Mendelssohn's atmospheric The Hebrides, which evokes Scotland's rugged coastline with dark, rolling lines in the low strings set against shimmering winds and strings that suggest the sea air. The journey concludes with Haydn's jubilant Symphony No. 104—his final symphony—whose finale bursts with rustic, folk-inspired energy that resonates beautifully in the intimate acoustics of St. Mary's Catholic Church....

Breathe deeper. Move freer. Connect stronger.

Wild Women Tribe's fall Movement & Mindfulness Wed Weekly Trail Hike Series is back for the 4th season \(Wed 7/1 to Wed 8/5\)—six weeks of soul-fueled hikes, fresh air, and movement that awakens more than just your body.

It’s not just about the hike. It’s about the women walking beside you. The conversations that crack you open. The moments of presence & wonder. And the laughter that lingers long after the trail ends. Join our six-part hike series in Park City. We lace up and hit the dirt with a variety of modalities featuring local facilitators: from grounding somatic breathwork with Jilana McIntyre \(July 1\), a sacred blue lotus tea ceremony with Christina Sthair \(July 8\), to soul-soothing soundbath on the earth with Amanda Murphy \(July 29\), there's a little something for every woman seeking deep connection back to nature.

July 1: Jilana McIntyre \(somatic breathwork\)

July 8: Christina Sthair \(blue lotus tea ceremony\)

July 15: Sofia Mileti \(Foundation training\)

July 22: Renee Huang \(NLP style guided journal writing\)

July 29: Amanda Murphy \(soundbath meditation\)

You'll learn how to prevent the bleach from putting holes in your clothing, and then use professional-grade dyes to create your own custom color palette. You'll leave with speciality detergent and instructions to thoroughly wash your tie dye at home. Note: Using bleach to remove color is optional! You can bring white or light-colored items to this class. IMPORTANT: Please bring your own clothing to dye! Please limit yourself to 3 small items, like t-shirts or shorts, OR 1 large item, like a sweatshirt. MOST IMPORTANT: Items MUST be 100% cotton for best results. 80% cotton will work, but is less ideal. We do not recommend bringing clothing items that are less than 70% cotton. If you are unsure about an item, we recommend bringing something else. For color removal, the brand Comfort Colors is NOT recommended! The Trash Pile offers sustainably sourced, one-of-a-kind tie-dye. Each item is carefully selected at a local thrift store and is then thoughtfully tied and dyed by hand into a wearable work of art. Since launching in 2021, The Trash Pile has diverted more than 5,000 pieces of clothing from landfills. What began as a pandemic hobby is now a growing movement to save the planet, one t-shirt at a time. ACE aims to create an inclusive and accessible environment for all of our attendees; please contact our Executive Director, Sara Gibbs, with any questions regarding accessibility....

Walker Hayes returns with his most introspective and heartfelt project yet, 17 Problems, an album shaped by reflection, resilience, and raw honesty. Blending hip-hop-infused production with country storytelling, Hayes dives deep into themes of fatherhood, faith, grief, and growth. From the aching vulnerability of “17 Year Old Problems” and “Song for My Son” to the high-energy anthems “Mother” and “Neon Lights,” the album captures the full spectrum of life’s beauty and messiness. With over 100 songs written for this release, Hayes carefully curated 17 tracks that reveal the most personal side of his artistry to date, working with top collaborators like Warren “Oak” Felder, Shane McAnally, and Bart Millard while also penning deeply personal solo material.

 

To bring this story to life, Hayes has announced the Walker Hayes Unplugged Tour, where he offers fans an intimate, acoustic experience unlike anything he’s done before. Stripping back the production to let the lyrics lead, Hayes takes audiences on a journey through the highs and lows that shaped him - from viral fame to quiet family moments, from deep heartbreak to enduring faith. Through heartfelt storytelling and soul-stirring songs, this special evening invites fans into the heart of his story. More than a concert, it’s a celebration of connection, resilience, and the messy, beautiful reality of life, one song at a time....

events.title: Beethoven's Symphony No. 7
events.description: Promising a night of lyrical beauty and orchestral drama, conductor Louis Lohraseb shapes a program that follows an arc of adoration to heartbreak in the first half. The season finale at St. Mary's Catholic Church opens with Wagner's tender Siegfried Idyll, a deeply personal expression of love written as a birthday gift for his wife. Then the spotlight turns to Erica Petrocelli in two dramatic works that showcase the brilliance and expressive power of the soprano voice: Mozart's virtuosic “Come scoglio” from Così fan tutte, a declaration of unwavering fidelity, and Mendelsohn&\#03's “Infelice,” where sweet memories offer fleeting comfort after a lover's betrayal.Famously called “the apotheosis of the dance itself” by Wagner, Beethoven's Symphony No. 7 brings the night to a triumphant close. An instant symphonic favorite—with early audiences reportedly demanding a repeat of the second movement—the piece surges with wildness and joy, culminating in one of the most electrifying finales in classical music....

events.title: Lunch and Learn - Exploring Energy Strategies for your Business
events.description:
Join the Park City // Summit County Green Business Program on Wednesday, August 12 at the Park City Chamber from 12 pm to 1 pm to discover the role renewable energy can play as one of many strategies businesses can use to understand, reduce, and transform the energy used in their day-to-day operations. Join experts from Vote Solar**,** Summit County, and U-Crew, as they discuss the benefits, share success stories, and highlight ways businesses can become more involved in clean and renewable energy initiatives.

During the session, speakers will discuss the different approaches businesses can take to meet their energy goals, explain the differences between renewable and clean energy, address common energy-related challenges, and highlight current and upcoming Rocky Mountain Power programs. Lunch is provided!

Featured Speakers include:

Creed McCord, Program Engineer at U-Crew, will share a local program available to businesses seeking to better understand and reduce their energy use.

Kate Bowman, Regulatory Director at Vote Solar, will discuss the role renewable energy can play in helping businesses achieve their sustainability goals.

Emily Quinton, Summit County Sustainability Director and Secretary of the Utah Renewable Communities Board, will provide the big-picture framework for business energy decision-making. She will introduce the energy hierarchy, explain the differences between clean and renewable energy, and discuss the range of utility-scale energy options available to commercial customers. Emily will also provide an overview of the new Community Clean Energy Program, adopted by Summit County, Park City, Francis, and Oakley, and what it means for local businesses and the future of clean energy in Utah.

Register at parkcitygreen.org/events...

events.title: Chef’s Table x Park City Community Foundation
events.description:
Join **Chef's Table** and **Park City Community Foundation** for an intimate evening benefiting our **Zero Food Waste initiative**, hosted at Alpinist in Deer Valley. This small, chef-driven dinner brings together food lovers, community supporters, and celebrated culinary voices for a night of connection, purpose, delicious food - and zero food waste. Guests will enjoy an intentional menu with courses developed by world-renowned **Chef Inés Páez Nin**, **Chef Jaime Rodríguez,** and chefs from Alpinist, alongside a wine pairing led by vintners from Redhawk Vineyard. Proceeds from the event benefit Park City Community Foundation's Zero Food Waste initiative, which is working to eliminate food waste from the Summit County landfill by 2030. We have already diverted over 1,000 tons of food waste and are establishing programs for both residential and commercial food waste pick up.

Join us to connect directly with chefs who are putting sustainability into practice in their own kitchens, and to support that same work happening right here at home.

*Please note, this event is 21+ only.*...
events.location: Alpinist, Park City, UT

events.title: Terence Hansen Solo
events.description: For over 20 years virtuoso guitarist/singer/songwriter/producer, Terence Hansen, has been performing his own compositions, popular standards, and classics to audiences in the USA and Europe using his version of the tapping technique on two guitars simultaneously \(while singing\). Terence's music has pop, prog rock, jazz, funk, Latin, ambient, and blues influences, with lyrics and vocals reminiscent of Pink Floyd. Terence performs on his unique Dutch-made custom built 'crossed neck' acoustic and electric Heeres guitars. Terence's unusual approach to guitar playing has been featured on tracks with Rik Hoogendoorn \(actor\), Richard Heijerman \(Herman Brood\), Rich Wyman \(Van Halen\), Jos Van Oost, Isaiah Stewart, Randy Brecker \(Brecker Brothers\), Tom Scott \(Joni Mitchell\), Deodato \(Earth Wind and Fire\), and Jamie Glaser \(Jean Luc Ponty\), Hugh McDonald \(Bon Jovi\), as well as movie soundtracks, toys, aquariums', and commercials. Terence has opened for artists such as Robert Palmer, Jennifer Batten, Gary Hoey, Neil Zaza, Bumblefoot, as well as headlined Zappanale 22 \(Germany\), the Spijkenisse Festival \(Holland\), the Den Haag Guitar Festival, Guitar Nation \(London\), Hellevoutsluis Guitar Festival, and has been featured in GitaarPlus Magazine and recently GuitarWorld.com. Terence was also a subject of the Dutch made documentary film, 'Two Men and Their Guitarz' \(2017\), and is featured in the concert movie, 'BeatALS' \(2018\). Terence's 10th album, 'Baktune' \(2018\) is his first purely instrumental album with his crossed neck acoustic guitar trio. Terence was recently awarded 'Best Independent Live Artist of 2019' by Scorpius Magazine....

events.title: fearless abstract painting
events.description: fearless abstract painting Tuesday , August 18th | 6PM | Alta Peruvian Lawn | $15 | Sign-up Required In this class, students will learn how to create fearless, intuitive abstract paintings using Samantha da Silva's signature "no rules" roller-painting method, incorporating plaster, salt, sand, sawdust, and playful canvas manipulation techniques. This class is especially good for people who want to learn how to silence their inner critic, overcome fear of the blank canvas, trust their intuition, and discover their own authentic artistic voice in a joyful, judgment-free space. You will use rollers \(instead of brushes\), large quantities of acrylic paint and water, plaster, salt, sand, sawdust, and your hands directly on the canvas laid flat on a table. At the end of the class, you will leave with one completed, textured abstract painting, a toolbox of fearless techniques you can use forever, and the confidence to keep creating without rules or self-doubt. Samantha da Silva \(b. 1978, Brazil\) is a Brazilian-born, Salt Lake City-based artist and dedicated educator who has taught visual arts for over twenty years in public and private schools and institutions across Canada, the United States, Hawaii, and France. Shaped by nearly forty moves triggered by natural disasters and life circumstances, and by the intense assimilation she experienced at age ten, da Silva channels themes of migration, belonging, and resourcefulness into her widely recognized large-scale relief sculptures-topographic-like works built from found dirt, sawdust, and debris-that have appeared in Architectural Digest, Bravo TV, and HGTV. In the classroom, she guides students of all ages to transform personal experience and everyday materials into powerful expression, making art a vital tool for connection and resilience in an ever-shifting world. ACE aims to create an inclusive and accessible environment for all of our attendees; please contact our Executive Director, Sara Gibbs, with any questions...

Featuring Ayja Bounous and Teri Harman, writers and contributors to the anthology The Once and Future Lake: Stories for Great Salt Lake; Jake Dreyfous, managing director of Grow the Flow; and Jack Stauss, Executive Director of Save Our Canyons; and moderated by Torrey House Press Executive Director Kirsten Johanna Allen, LAKE EFFECT invites a community discussion on how to maintain a legacy of winter for future generations. ABOUT THE PANELISTS: Kirsten Johanna Allen \(she/her\) directs acquisitions, editing, production, and marketing for Torrey House Press with co-executive director Will Neville-Rehbehn. As co-founder, Kirsten has steered the press from its earliest inklings to publish conservation through literature to become the powerful platform for books and ideas about the natural world and the West that it is today. Kirsten holds a BA from Westminster College and an MPH from the University of Utah. She has two grown children and lives with a pair of cats and her spouse, Mark Bailey, in Salt Lake City and Torrey, Utah. Ayja Bounous is a Salt Lake City-based writer inspired by water in all its forms. events.title: Saloons and Saloon Keepers of Park City by Sandy Brumley and Jane Perkins
events.description:
Park City Museum will host a lecture called ***Saloons and Saloon Keepers of Parley’s Park City*** given by Sandy Brumley and Jane Perkins on Wednesday, September 2, 2026 from 5-6 p.m. held at the Education and Collections Center located at 2079 Sidewinder Drive. More information can be found at www.parkcityhistory.org.

Saloons were a cornerstone social institution in every western mining camp and Parley’s Park City, as our town was known in its earliest days, was no exception. Two of “The Park’s” earliest saloon keepers were Thomas Cupit and Jack Pape, who were also The Justice of the Peace and Deputy Sheriff, respectively.  While saloons tended to come and go with their saloon keepers, there were usually somewhere between fifteen and thirty saloons active in the camp at any given time.

Cupit and Pape, who were partners in an earlier saloon in Salt Lake City, each operated his own establishment in The Park from the late 1870s up until about 1910, when Jack Pape left for the Yukon.  During that period, there were over thirty murders in and around The Park, many of them occurring in various saloons, including The Cupit & Brennan Saloon.  Jack Pape’s Grizzly Saloon figured prominently in the famous Black Jack Murphy murder/lynching.

Jane Perkins and Sandy Brumley will describe the historic arc etched by Cupit and Pape, as well as their contemporaries.  Jane will provide her perspective as a founder of the High West Saloon and Distillery while Sandy will add facts around the 19th century newspapers to uncover many of the stories from this era.

A mountain host and hiking guide at Park City Mountain Resort, Sandy Brumley is a descendent of iron miners in Minnesota and an avid student of Park City History.  This will be the seventh in a series of presentations he has made for the Museum.  He is a hike leader for the Museum and a member of Friends of Ski Mountain Mining History.

Jane Perkins' love of Park City’s history began when she and her husband moved here ful...

events.title: Terence Hansen Solo
events.description: For over 20 years virtuoso guitarist/singer/songwriter/producer, Terence Hansen, has been performing his own compositions, popular standards, and classics to audiences in the USA and Europe using his version of the tapping technique on two guitars simultaneously \(while singing\). Terence's music has pop, prog rock, jazz, funk, Latin, ambient, and blues influences, with lyrics and vocals reminiscent of Pink Floyd. Terence performs on his unique Dutch-made custom built 'crossed neck' acoustic and electric Heeres guitars. Terence's unusual approach to guitar playing has been featured on tracks with Rik Hoogendoorn \(actor\), Richard Heijerman \(Herman Brood\), Rich Wyman \(Van Halen\), Jos Van Oost, Isaiah Stewart, Randy Brecker \(Brecker Brothers\), Tom Scott \(Joni Mitchell\), Deodato \(Earth Wind and Fire\), and Jamie Glaser \(Jean Luc Ponty\), Hugh McDonald \(Bon Jovi\), as well as movie soundtracks, toys, aquariums', and commercials. Terence has opened for artists such as Robert Palmer, Jennifer Batten, Gary Hoey, Neil Zaza, Bumblefoot, as well as headlined Zappanale 22 \(Germany\), the Spijkenisse Festival \(Holland\), the Den Haag Guitar Festival, Guitar Nation \(London\), Hellevoutsluis Guitar Festival, and has been featured in GitaarPlus Magazine and recently GuitarWorld.com. Terence was also a subject of the Dutch made documentary film, 'Two Men and Their Guitarz' \(2017\), and is featured in the concert movie, 'BeatALS' \(2018\). Terence's 10th album, 'Baktune' \(2018\) is his first purely instrumental album with his crossed neck acoustic guitar trio. Terence was recently awarded 'Best Independent Live Artist of 2019' by Scorpius Magazine....

Park City Museum and Friends of Ski Mountain Mining History will host a lecture called *Showcasing Park City’s Silver Mining Past with the Historic Mine Route Project* given by Wayne McKay on Wednesday, September 9, 2026 from 5-6 p.m. held at the Education and Collections Center located at 2079 Sidewinder Drive. More information can be found at www.parkcityhistory.org.

The Historic Mine Route (HMR) project creates a self-guided, audio-assisted tour of over 20 historic mine sites in the mountains surrounding Park City. The HMR brings together outdoor recreation, historic preservation, storytelling, and sustainable tourism into one experience that is uniquely Park City. Visitors are not just hiking; they are walking through the mining history that shaped this community.  The presentation will focus on how Park City is attracting heritage tourism to reclaimed abandoned silver mine sites after they have been made safe for the public to visit.

Wayne McKay has a BSc and MSc in Petroleum Engineering from Stanford University.  He was employed by Chevron and Cenovus Energy in multiple domestic and international locations.  He moved to Park City in 2019 and is enjoying retirement, volunteering for the Park City Historical Society & Museum, as well as working part-time as a ski instructor at Park City Mountain Resort. He has enjoyed his role as a volunteer in Friends of Ski Mountain Mining History, helping to make Park City's mining history stories more available and interesting to locals and visitors....

events.title: A.J. Croce Presents CROCE PLAYS CROCE
events.description:
According to Willie Nelson, “A.J. Croce has wisdom beyond his years. With his music, he represents his generation with a profound sense of honesty in his lyrics and quality in his delivery. The future of entertainment is safe in his hands!”    

Some artists are afforded the chance to tell their personal stories as they see fit, at a particular moment when they know the time has come. But for many, there is no choice — the story emerges hardwired to the music and they become forever identified with it no matter how their story may evolve or change.

A.J. Croce has been inextricably linked to a version of his own story by virtue of his name. He’s experienced a lifetime of comparisons to a father he lost at age two, whose music bears little resemblance to his own output yet still serves as a reference point despite the years that have passed and the many iconic mentors who have stepped in to offer their counsel, creativity, and endorsement throughout his long career.

It’s curious that it now feels necessary to include the reference, as enough time has passed that a new generation of tastemakers and journalists might not know who Jim Croce was — that he was a golden-voiced everyman, a singer-songwriter-guitarist who died too soon, leaving one of pop music’s most beautiful and memorable ballads \(written about a young A.J.\) in his wake.

Croce the younger, on the other hand, is a piano man, first and foremost, and a vocal stylist second. His muted growl pulls from a host of American traditions and anti-heroes — it’s part New Orleans, part juke joint, part soul, but somehow evokes New York, a continuum where John Lurie meets Lou Reed. He is further a songwriter, driven by a personal muse, informed by a life on a boomerang of tragedy.

His gritty and accomplished ninth studio album, produced by legendary soul singer-songwriter and producer Dan Penn, is the latest and arguably greatest effort yet. Penn, of course, is writer of such hits as “The Dark End of the Street,...

events.title: Gorgeous Gourds
events.description:
Psychedelic Funk band Gorgeous Gourds combine smooth harmonies, deep tasty grooves, and original songwriting.

The Gorgeous Gourd's just released album \(2/22/22\) "Peace and Love" reminds us why we go see and hear live music. The band has evolved to a rock solid synergistic group of accomplished musicians. Their powerful singing and songwriting is evident on their new CD, with 14 worthy cuts combining an eclectic combination of psychedelic funk, folk, tasty jam grooves, smooth harmonies and soulful ballads. Fred, Lucas, and Sarah all share the artful original songwriting. Iconic KRCL DJ John Florence commented on the new album, "Not a stinker in the bunch!”

Formed in Salt Lake City, Utah in 2015, founding members are Fred Hayes \(bass, vocals\), and the strong and steady Bob Smith \(drums\). Lucas Jones \(lead guitar,vocals\) provides sublime and powerful guitar licks and vocals, together with the guitar of Jacob Dahlberg and the dazzling vocals of Heather McCartin. 

Whether you enjoy easing into a bluesy flow ride, or getting all the kinks out on the dance floor, the Gorgeous Gourds is the party you'll keep coming back to. The title of their new album "Peace and Love" is a message they spread with unbridled energy and enthusiasm.

Like they say, "You're Gorgeous, we're the Gourds. Together we are Gorgeous Gourds."

Terence was also a subject of the Dutch made documentary film, 'Two Men and Their Guitarz' \(2017\), and is featured in the concert movie, 'BeatALS' \(2018\). Terence's 10th album, 'Baktune' \(2018\) is his first purely instrumental album with his crossed neck acoustic guitar trio. events.title: Mason Jennings
events.description:
Mason Jennings is a Minnesota-based pop-folk singer-songwriter. Jennings is originally from Honolulu, Hawaii. He is well known for his simple yet catchy melodies, intimate lyrics, intensely literary and historical themes, and deep tenor's voice. His music has appeared in the surf film Shelter and he has toured extensively. Jennings is married to Amy Jennings \(nee Turany\) and has a son, August, born in January 2003.

 

 Jennings produced his self-titled debut album in 1997 on an analog four-track in the basement of a rented home, manning all instruments himself. In October 1998, after bringing drummer Chris Stock and bassist Robert Skoro on board, he began a weekly gig at Minneapolis' 400 Bar as the Mason Jennings Band. Garnering local praise and a wide fan base, Mason began touring nationally.

 

 His 2000 album Birds Flying Away revealed Jennings' political activism and penchant for singing first-person narratives of imaginary rustic characters. Following the release of this album, Noah Levy took over drumming duties from Stock.

 

 2002 saw the release of two albums: the studio piece Century Spring and a "fans only" collection of acoustic rarities, Simple Life. An EP supporting Century Spring was also released, featuring the album's opening track, "Living In The Moment," two live tracks, and the previously-unreleased "Emperor Ashoka." Jennings released all three discs -- and re-released his earlier albums -- on his homebrewed record label, Architect Records.

 

 In 2003, Skoro and Levy left the band \(the former to pursue a solo career\), and were replaced by bassist Chris Morrissey \(formerly of Bill Mike Band\) and drummer Brian Mcleod.

 

 On 10 February 2004, Jennings released Use Your Voice, which notably included the songs "Keepin' It Real," a foot-stomper ostensibly written at the request of Shrek 2 producers \(but not used in the film\), and "The Ballad of Paul and Sheila," an acoustic dirge for l...

events.title: Mason Jennings
events.description:
Mason Jennings is a Minnesota-based pop-folk singer-songwriter. Jennings is originally from Honolulu, Hawaii. He is well known for his simple yet catchy melodies, intimate lyrics, intensely literary and historical themes, and deep tenor's voice. His music has appeared in the surf film Shelter and he has toured extensively. Jennings is married to Amy Jennings \(nee Turany\) and has a son, August, born in January 2003.

 

 Jennings produced his self-titled debut album in 1997 on an analog four-track in the basement of a rented home, manning all instruments himself. In October 1998, after bringing drummer Chris Stock and bassist Robert Skoro on board, he began a weekly gig at Minneapolis' 400 Bar as the Mason Jennings Band. Garnering local praise and a wide fan base, Mason began touring nationally.

 

 His 2000 album Birds Flying Away revealed Jennings' political activism and penchant for singing first-person narratives of imaginary rustic characters. Following the release of this album, Noah Levy took over drumming duties from Stock.

 

 2002 saw the release of two albums: the studio piece Century Spring and a "fans only" collection of acoustic rarities, Simple Life. An EP supporting Century Spring was also released, featuring the album's opening track, "Living In The Moment," two live tracks, and the previously-unreleased "Emperor Ashoka." Jennings released all three discs -- and re-released his earlier albums -- on his homebrewed record label, Architect Records.

 

 In 2003, Skoro and Levy left the band \(the former to pursue a solo career\), and were replaced by bassist Chris Morrissey \(formerly of Bill Mike Band\) and drummer Brian Mcleod.

 

 On 10 February 2004, Jennings released Use Your Voice, which notably included the songs "Keepin' It Real," a foot-stomper ostensibly written at the request of Shrek 2 producers \(but not used in the film\), and "The Ballad of Paul and Sheila," an acoustic dirge for l...

events.title: secrets below alta: wild west archaeology in a mining boom town
events.description: secrets below alta: wild west archaeology in a mining boom town Thursday, October 22nd | Our Lady of the Snows | 6PM | Free | Sign-up Required If you love Old West ghost-town history, you won't want to miss this! For the first time ever, the mining boomtown of Alta has been partially excavated and what emerged from the ground is incredible. Thousands of artifacts were uncovered, including a fully intact bottle of 150-year-old alcohol, a leather hat, bullets, melted shot glasses, animal bones and so much more. Discover what these objects reveal about the rowdy and genteel past of Little Cottonwood Canyon. Christopher Merritt received his Ph.D. from the University of Montana in Anthropology in 2010, focusing on archaeological and historical investigations of the Overseas Chinese. Before that, he received a Master's of Science in Industrial Archaeology from Michigan Technological University, where he studied the trade and consumption of Mormon-produced pottery in Utah. Since 2004, Merritt has worked in a variety of professional archaeological settings, including the United States Forest Service in Utah and Nevada, private archaeological contracting in Salt Lake City, and, finally, as the State Historic Preservation Officer for the Utah Division of State History. In addition to the full-time employment with the State of Utah, he is Adjunct Faculty in Anthropology at Salt Lake Community College and an instructor for the Osher Lifelong Learning Institute. ACE aims to create an inclusive and accessible environment for all of our attendees; please contact our Executive Director, Sara Gibbs, with any questions regarding accessibility....

events.title: Country Weekend - Lonestar
events.description:
Lonestar is a celebrated American country music group that earned global recognition with their timeless ballad “Amazed,” a crossover sensation that dominated the charts for 9 weeks at No. 1 on the country charts and 2 weeks at No. 1 on the pop charts. Known for blending heartfelt storytelling with a polished pop-country sound, the band — comprised of Dean Sams, Michael Britt, Keech Rainwater, and Drew Womack — has made a lasting impact on the genre.
With an impressive 22 top ten singles on the Billboard Hot Country Songs chart, including 10 that reached No. 1, Lonestar has built one of the most successful track records in modern country music. Their rise began in 1995 with the top-five single “Tequila Talking,” followed by chart-topping hits such as the rock-tinged “No News,” “Come Cryin’ to Me,” and “Everything’s Changed.”
The release of their quadruple-platinum 1999 album Lonely Grill firmly established their legacy, producing four No. 1 singles and showcasing the band’s signature ability to craft emotionally resonant, radio-friendly songs.
Lonestar’s achievements have earned them widespread acclaim, including multiple Academy of Country Music awards for New Vocal Group, Single of the Year, Song of the Year, and Humanitarian of the Year. They have also been honored by the Country Music Association with Vocal Group of the Year and the International Artist Achievement Award.
With more than 10.5 million records sold worldwide, Lonestar remains one of country music’s most enduring and influential bands, continuing to inspire fans with their heartfelt hits and remarkable musical legacy.

events.description:
Country superstar Walker Hayes is a singer-songwriter from Mobile, Alabama, known for blending country storytelling with pop and hip-hop-inspired production. His latest project, 17 Problems, is his most personal work to date—an introspective album shaped by resilience, faith, family, grief, and growth. Featuring both high-energy anthems and deeply emotional storytelling, the album highlights Hayes’ evolution as an artist and songwriter.
Known for his authenticity and engaging live performances, Hayes has appeared on Good Morning America, The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon, Late Night with Seth Meyers, TODAY, and CBS Sunday Morning. Whether delivering chart-topping hits or stripped-down acoustic moments, Walker Hayes invites audiences into a powerful, honest, and unforgettable live experience.

events.title: Richard Marx
events.description: Richard Marx is a Grammy-winning singer, songwriter, and producer whose career has spanned four decades of chart success and creative reinvention. With over 45 million albums sold, one billion streams, and fourteen No. 1 singles to his name (including "Right Here Waiting," "Hazard" & "Hold On to the Nights"), Marx is the only male artist in history to have his first seven singles reach the Top 5 on the Billboard charts, and one of only two artists—alongside Michael Jackson—to write a No. 1 song in four different decades. Marx's work extends far beyond his own recordings; he has written and produced for artists including Luther Vandross, Keith Urban, NSYNC, Barbra Streisand and Burt Bacharach. His latest album After Hours (featuring Rod Stewart & Kenny G) debuted at No. 14 on Billboard’s Traditional Jazz Albums chart and was praised by The New York Times, USA Today, Billboard & more. He hosts the hit podcast Stories To Tell (with guests including Paul Stanley, Rick Springfield & Kenny Loggins) and lives with his wife, Cuban-American TV host Daisy Fuentes, in Malibu, CA.

events.title: Colin Cloud: Mastermind
events.description:
Step into the mind-bending world of Colin Cloud, often called the “real-life Sherlock Holmes.”
 
In Mastermind, Cloud combines razor-sharp wit, jaw-dropping mentalism, and astonishing deduction to create an evening that is as hilarious as it is mystifying. Fast-paced, funny, and endlessly surprising, the show turns the audience into the star—inviting volunteers on stage for impossible reveals, uncanny predictions, and secrets no one thought could be known. Critics rave that Cloud is “slick, skillful, and utterly compelling,” and fans describe the experience as “stunning, engaging, and full of surprises.” Mastermind is more than a performance—it’s a thrilling journey into the limits of the human mind, guaranteed to leave you laughing, gasping, and questioning everything you thought was possible.

events.description: Join us for a weekend of brews! — Experience the Deer Valley Mountain Beer Festival on Saturday and Sunday, September 19 and 20, from 12 to 5 p.m. Enjoy live music from Dylan Catrone on Saturday and G. Love & Special Sauce on Sunday, along with scenic chairlift access throughout the resort, outdoor dining, and family-friendly activities. Sample a curated selection of Utah’s finest craft beers, including full-strength varieties, and discover diverse styles from beloved local breweries. Please note: festival access is only available via a chairlift ride on Silver Lake Express, with parking and check-in at Snow Park Lodge. September 19 September 20
events.location: Silver Lake Base Area, Deer Valley, Park City, UT
